newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn seen one to two cents up on cool weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn seen one to two cents up on cool weather.

text.p: CBOT corn futures were expected to open one to two cents per bushel higher on weather concerns and spillover from overnight trade, traders said.
The latest 6- to 10-day forecast from the National Weather Service showed below normal temperatures for much of the U.S. Midwest.
"There are still worries over emergence," a trader said.
The cool forecasts were generating concern over corn emergence and growth and in turn, supporting prices, traders said.
However, on Monday, USDA rated the U.S. corn crop 60 percent good to excellent compared with 51 percent in that category a year ago.
Some buying triggered by gains in overnight trade was also seen early. On Project A, corn futures settled 3/4 to two cents per bushel higher.
